# The audit index

**GENERATED. Do not edit this file by hand.** Every row is derived from
the corpus by `scripts/build_audit_index.py`;
`tests/test_the_audit_index_is_derived.py` re-derives it and fails on any
drift, so an edit here is a change that will be reverted by the next
regeneration rather than a change to the record.

    python scripts/build_audit_index.py --write

**THE DOMAIN IS WHAT GIT TRACKS UNDER `_audit`**, not what is on disk.
`_audit/_scratch/` is gitignored, so a disk walk would index documents no
clone has -- the exact divergence that made the correction guard pass
locally and fail in a clone at the same SHA.

**WHAT THIS FILE CANNOT TELL YOU.** Whether a document is still true. Only
a `CORRECTS:` / `CORRECTED BY:` marker somebody wrote can say that, and
section 2 below is exactly those markers and nothing inferred. A document
absent from section 2 is a document nobody has declared a correction of --
which is not the same as one nobody has overtaken.

Dates come from the `YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix. Documents without one
are listed as `(undated)`; no date is taken from git history, because
`git ls-files` works in a shallow clone and `git log` does not.

**THE MARKER LINES OUTNUMBER THE EDGES**, because some pairs are
declared more than once, for two different claims. Every reason is
printed below; a pair-keyed dictionary keeps only the last of each,
which is how those reasons went unread.

## 2. What a later document corrected

**A reader who arrives at a claim should be able to see here, without
grep, that something later overtook it.** Each entry is the corrected
document, then the correctors it names, then the reason THAT DOCUMENT
ITSELF gives -- quoted from its own `CORRECTED BY:` line, not summarised.

A correction is of a CLAIM, never of a whole document. Nothing here says a
document is dead; it says one thing in it was overtaken and names what.

boundary in prose is how a reason becomes a fragment.

## 6. What the scan rejected, could not join, or had to repair

**An empty section here would be a claim, so it is printed only when
there is something in it.** Everything below is a thing somebody
should look at; none of it is absorbed silently.

`tests/test_a_correction_is_findable_from_the_claim.py::_reason_on`
reads ONE PHYSICAL LINE, and this corpus hard-wraps prose at about
78 columns. The markers below write their reason across several
lines, so everything past the first is outside its reach. **Sections
2, 3 and 4 above print the whole paragraph.**

This is not the last-backtick defect, which was fixed upstream on
2026-09-20. It is a different class, and the suffix property that
closed the first one cannot see it: that test compares one line
against the same line, so a missing continuation satisfies it.
